Q: How can I find processes based on port and kill them all? A:

Use:

... | awk '{ print $4 }' | xargs kill -9

Please test with "echo" instead of "kill" before running it.

Q: How can I kill a process running on particular port in Linux? A:

This prints the process ids of everything running on <port_number> to standard output:

fuser -n tcp <port_number>

It also prints some stuff to standard error, so:

fuser -n tcp <port_number> 2> /dev/null

We can then supply these process ids to the kill command:

sudo kill $(fuser -n tcp <port_number> 2> /dev/null)

You could also put this in a function if you do it a lot:

function killport() {
    sudo kill $(fuser -n tcp $1 2> /dev/null)
}

Q: ImportError in old migrations (django.utils.timezone.utc) after upgrading Python and Django A:

it is safe to modify an old migration if you are only fixing the import, not changing the migration logic.

the clean fix is to update the migration from:

from django.utils.timezone import utc

to:

import datetime
utc = datetime.timezone.utc

This is usually safe as it doesn't alter the migration's work or the state of the database it only changes a path of an import that has been removed.

I would avoid monkey-patching django.utils.timezone.utc in manage.py / wsgi.py except as a temporary workaround, because it hides the actual compatibility issue and makes the project depend on runtime patching.

Q: Resizing two shapes simultaneously over time A:

You can adjust both shapes within the same loop:

Sub Curtains()
    Const DELAY_SEC As Double = 0.001  'sec delay for each resizing
    Const END_WIDTH As Long = 30       'final width for shapes
    
    Dim shpL As Shape, shpR As Shape, ws As Worksheet
    Dim starttime As Double, pos As Long

    Set ws = ActiveSheet
    Set shpL = ws.Shapes("Rectangle 6")   'left-hand shape
    Set shpR = ws.Shapes("Rectangle 7")   'right-hand shape
    pos = shpR.left + shpR.Width          'starting right edge position of shpR
    
    'loop until at least one shape meets the ending width
    Do While shpL.Width > END_WIDTH And shpR.Width > END_WIDTH
        
        shpL.Width = shpL.Width - 1 'resize the left shape
        
        With shpR                   'resize the right shape
            .Width = .Width - 1
            .Left = pos - .Width    'reposition the right edge 
        End With                    ' (shape is resized from the right)
        
        starttime = Timer 'watch out for midnight here!
        Do
            DoEvents
        Loop While Timer - starttime < DELAY_SEC
    Loop
End Sub

Q: Pick a random value from an enum? A:

ThreadLocalRandom

Wow, so many Answers that try too hard.

Here is a concise, easy, thread-safe approach using ThreadLocalRandom.

enum Letter { A , B , C }

Select one enum object randomly.

  • All the constant objects of an enum class can be obtained by calling the implicit public static T[] values() method of that class, returning an array. (A fact unfortunately buried in the Javadoc.)
  • ThreadLocalRandom.current() returns the current thread's ThreadLocalRandom object, a random number generator isolated that particular thread. So, thread-safe, without contention.
  • ThreadLocalRandom offers the handy nextInt method taking only the bound while assuming an origin of zero. Just what we need to access a zero-based index into an array.
Letter randomLetter = 
    Letter                                   // Your `enum` class.
        .values()                            // Returns an array of all the objects defined in your enum.                                       
        [                                    // Square-bracket accesses an element from the array using zero-based index counting.
            ThreadLocalRandom                // A random-number generator local to a particular thread.
                .current()                   // Access the current thread’s random generator. Thread-safe, without contention.
                .nextInt(                    // Generate an `int` number in range of zero (inclusive) to specified bound (exclusive, Half-Open). 
                    Letter.values().length   // Size of array.
                )                            // Returns an `int`, our index into array of enum objects. 
        ]                                    // Returns the randomly-selected object from the enum.
;

You could easily use that code as a one-liner, wherever you need it. Or we could make a handy little class, with a tiny bit of optimization by caching the array of enums (though a JDK implementation may already be doing that, I don’t know).

By the way, in Java 16+, you can define an enum locally in addition to a nested or separate class. (See JEP 395.)
